_comment: ngsolve stokes#5 (NGSolve Stokes uses the +p*div(v) convention, opposite sign from FEniCS / skfem). Run 2026-08-06 on NGSolve 6.2.2604: plane Poiseuille in a 4x1 channel, nu=1, parabolic inlet peak 1, traction-free outlet, Taylor-Hood order 2/1, maxh 0.2, the two runs differing ONLY in the sign of the two coupling terms. TWO CORRECTIONS. (a) The Signal is written as a cross-solver comparison and can only be checked by someone who also has FEniCS. It does not need to be: plane Poiseuille has the analytic gradient dp/dx = -8*nu*Umax/H^2 = -8, and one solver settles it. (b) 'Both are valid weak forms' is true of the VELOCITY and misleading about the pressure. Both conventions give umax = 0.99974 and velocity vectors identical to 0.0, but -p*div(v) returns dp/dx = -8.00000, matching the analytic sign, while +p*div(v) returns +8.00000 -- the same magnitude with the wrong sign, and the two pressure vectors sum to exactly 0.0 pointwise. An agent reporting the +convention field as 'the pressure' reports the wrong sign of a physical quantity, silently. The catalog's own NGSolve stokes generator emits 'a += div(u)*q*dx + div(v)*p*dx', read out of the generated source, so the shipped template is the + convention. Mutation: making both runs use the same sign removes the contrast and the fixture fails on plus_convention_has_the_wrong_sign.
